messages:
incident-bot: Paging @maya (oncall) for P99 latency SLO breach — customer GammaCorp — dedicated VPC pool us-west1-gamma. Detected p95 400ms -> p99 2.4s across /v1/generate. Alert: sustained for 8m. Link: https://redwood.metrics/alerts/1765123456 :rotating_light:

maya: I'm on it. grabbing runbooks. can someone post subset of affected host ids?

jessie: seeing a spike on pool 'dedicated-usw1-gamma'. host ids: gpu-034, gpu-045, gpu-046. p99 spike coincides with increased request rate from tenant token gamma-main-01.

ashish: (typo) @ashish — I'm seeing a big burst from co-tenant alpha-analytics around same time, many long context requests. Could be noisy neighbor.

ashish: sorry for the noise, meant to ping @ashish.

ashish: we should check prefix cache hit rates and KV cache evictions.

ashish: here are quick metrics: cache_hit_rate: 12% -> 5%, kv_evictions/sec: 142 -> 560, avg_seq_len_gamma: 512 -> 2048

maya: thanks. Actions: 1) isolate gamma traffic to fallback variant, 2) enable per-tenant rate limiting at ingress, 3) if needed spin up reserved burst nodes. Attempting 1 and 2 now.

lina: I'll open the canary route to route gamma to model: redwood/gamma-medium-quant (lower perf but stable). applying route patch now.

jessie: lina please paste the patch.

lina: ```
# kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: routing.redwood/v1
kind: Route
metadata:
  name: gamma-fallback
spec:
  tenant: gamma-main-01
  model: redwood/gamma-medium-quant
  weight: 100
```

lina: applied. waiting for endpoints to warm.

maya: enabling tenant rate limit 10 rps for gamma-main-01 at the edge. command: `rwctl tenant throttle set --tenant gamma-main-01 --rate 10 --burst 20`

opsbot: runbook step: notifying customer success. @carter (support) can you start comms?

carter (support): pinged GammaCorp SE (alice@gammacorp.com) — initial note sent: "We're seeing increased tail latency in your us-west deployment; we're isolating your traffic to a fallback model and applying temporary rate limits. Expect improved stability within 5-10m. We'll follow up with details."

evan: copying engineering summary to GammaCorp: impact p95 ~400ms, p99 ~2s for 8-12m window, mitigation: routed to fallback model + edge throttling. will send ETA for full remediation.

jessie: checking node metrics — gpu-045 shows sustained 95% SM utilization and high memcpy stalls. suspect model with long sequences filling KV cache.

maya: can we move traffic to reserved-burst-gamma pool? spinning up 2 nodes (a100-80gb) from Dedicated burst capacity. command: `infra scale dedicated-usw1-gamma +2 --type a100-80gb`

ashish: doing the scale now. should be live in ~4m. Also bumping default kv_cache_max_entries for gamma to 64k to reduce evictions: `rwctl config set --tenant gamma-main-01 kv_cache_max_entries=65536`

lina: route switch confirmed. p95 dropped to ~180ms, p99 down to ~560ms after fallback. still seeing occasional 1.2s tails.

maya: good. continue monitoring 10m. open question: why did alpha-analytics cause co-tenant eviction? need postmortem.

jessie: logs: ```
[2025-10-12T18:24:12Z] gpu-045 pid=4231 tenant=alpha-analytics seq_len=4096 tokens=1.2M
[2025-10-12T18:24:15Z] eviction: tenant=gamma-main-01 reason=kv_cache_pressure entries_evicted=1200
[2025-10-12T18:24:18Z] request_latency tenant=gamma-main-01 p99=2380ms
```

ashish: adding temporary tenant isolation rule to prevent alpha-analytics from hitting same cache slabs: `rwctl tenant isolate --tenant alpha-analytics --pool shared-slabs=false`

opsbot: NOTE: applied tenant isolation for alpha-analytics.

carter (support): GammaCorp acknowledged and appreciates the quick action. asked for timeline for permanent fix.

evan: propose permanent actions: 1) reserve dedicated slab for GammaCorp (kv cache partitioning), 2) quota controls per-tenant, 3) recommend GammaCorp use shorter context windows or prompt chunking. I'll propose these in the post-incident doc.

maya: scale finished +2 nodes, traffic steered. current p95 160ms, p99 420ms. I think we can mark mitigated.

incident-bot: Incident mitigation in progress. Status -> mitigated. Please ack when stable for 30m or confirm full resolution.

maya: ack, I'll keep monitoring. leaving this thread open for postmortem items.

jessie: adding blockers for postmortem: - lack of per-tenant KV partitioning - no automatic noisy-tenant throttling - we should have heuristic to detect long-seq storm and auto-isolate.

lina: creating ticket INF-1327 for KV partitioning and INF-1328 for noisy-tenant auto-throttle.

evan: I'll draft customer impact summary and remediation options, pinging @carter for approvals.

opsbot: Incident resolved by on-call. Closing window in 30m if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
